title: low-resource-vision finding
description: One record per experiment in findings.jsonl (JSON Lines: one object per line, no enclosing array). Written to be consumed by an AI agent deciding how to handle visual input. Each record is a hypothesis that was tested against pixels, and the verdict is usually REFUTED.

id.description: Stable identifier. Cited by this id in PAPER.md and AGENTS.md.

intent.description: Phrasings of what an agent might be ABOUT TO DO that lead here. This is the lookup key: match your own intention against these before acting, not after.

hypothesis.description: The belief under test, stated as the experimenter believed it before measuring.

method.description: What was actually done, including sample size. n=1 results were retracted; see F04.

measurement.description: Raw numbers and verbatim model outputs. Shape differs per finding by design — it mirrors the experiment, not a fixed table. Verbatim VLM outputs are quoted unedited, including the hallucinated people.

verdict.description: Outcome, opening with one of: REFUTED, CONFIRMED, CONDITIONAL, or a methodology failure. Eight of nine are not confirmations.

mechanism.description: Why the result came out that way. The transferable part — a verdict without a mechanism does not tell you whether it applies to your setup.

generalizes_to.description: The class of system the finding should hold for, and implicitly where it should not be trusted.

if_you_were_about_to.description: Direct instruction to an agent whose intention matched. Read this one if you read nothing else.

script.description: Repo-relative path to a runnable reproduction. Each script prints a 'RESULT: {json}' line on stdout so its outcome can be parsed without reading prose.
